facts.truth: In crm_contacts.csv one row is one contact record, but 80 people appear on more than one row.
In crm_deals.csv one row is one deal, keyed by Deal ID.
80 duplicate groups add 88 extra rows; the copies differ in email casing, a trailing space, title wording, phone format and Created. Dedupe on trimmed, lowercased email and keep the oldest row.
75 contact rows (5.0%) have no email: trade show badge scans.
Stage codes: S1 = new lead, not yet contacted; S2 = discovery call held, qualified; S3 = proposal sent; S4 = negotiation or verbal yes; S5 = customer (closed won).
Owner holds rep initials: JM = Jordan Mercer; AR = Alicia Reyes; KT = Kenji Tanaka; DL = Dana Lowe; SP = Sam Patel. JM (Jordan Mercer) left in March 2026 and 229 contacts were never reassigned.
Deals join contacts on Contact Email = Email: 85.0% match exactly, 92.0% after trimming and lowercasing, and 51 deals match nothing (personal addresses or blanks). 33 deals hit a duplicated contact.
Deal Amount is first-year contract value in USD; deal Stage uses words (Prospecting to Closed Lost) and is not synced with the contact S codes.
The Lead Source value "Web" was renamed "Website" on 2025-01-01; they mean the same thing.
230 contacts created before 2024 carry Created in M/D/YYYY format from the legacy CRM import; everything later is YYYY-MM-DD.
The owner wants a clean, deduplicated contact list before migrating CRMs in Q4 2026, a pipeline by source for the board, and JM's contacts reassigned.

owner_brief:
You are Jess Okafor, Sales Ops lead at Brightkeel Systems, a company that sells scheduling software to small service businesses. You exported crm_contacts.csv and crm_deals.csv from the CRM on September 22, 2026.

Contacts: one row per contact record. Stage codes are yours: S1 is a new lead not yet contacted, S2 means a discovery call was held and they are qualified, S3 means a proposal was sent, S4 is negotiation or a verbal yes, S5 is a customer. Owner is the rep's initials: JM is Jordan Mercer, AR Alicia Reyes, KT Kenji Tanaka, DL Dana Lowe, SP Sam Patel. Jordan left in March 2026 and nobody reassigned his contacts yet.

Duplicates: about 80 people are in there twice (a few three times), from a 2024 re-import and from reps adding people by hand. The copies usually differ in email capitalization or a stray space. Dedupe on the email trimmed and lowercased, and keep the oldest record.

Missing emails: around 5% of contacts have no email; those are trade show badge scans.

Dates: contacts created before 2024 came over from the legacy CRM in January 2024 and their Created dates are M/D/YYYY; everything since is YYYY-MM-DD.

Lead Source: "Web" was renamed "Website" on January 1, 2025. Same thing.

Deals: Contact Email is typed by the rep, so sometimes it is in capitals, sometimes it is the person's personal address, sometimes blank. Join on the trimmed, lowercased email; deals that match no contact are still real deals. Deal stages are words, separate from the S codes, and the two are not kept in sync. Amount is first-year contract value in USD.

Your goals: a clean deduplicated list before the CRM migration in Q4 2026, a pipeline by lead source for the board, and Jordan's contacts reassigned.

Answer only what you are asked, briefly. If something is not covered here, say "not sure".

eval_questions.q: How many distinct people are in crm_contacts.csv?
eval_questions.a: 1412: 1500 rows minus 88 duplicate rows (same email once trimmed and lowercased). The 75 rows with no email are counted one each.

eval_questions.q: How many duplicate contact groups are there, and how many extra rows do they add?
eval_questions.a: 80 groups (72 pairs and 8 triples) adding 88 extra rows; most differ only in email casing or a trailing space, 30 share the exact same email text.

eval_questions.q: What share of contact rows have no email address?
What share of deals match a contact by exact Contact Email, and what share after trimming and lowercasing both sides?
eval_questions.a: Exact: 85.0% (544 of 640). Normalized: 92.0% (589); 51 deals still match no contact (personal emails or blanks).

eval_questions.q: How many deals match more than one contact row after normalizing emails?
eval_questions.a: 33 deals point at a contact that exists on two or three rows, so a plain join would double count them.

eval_questions.q: How many distinct contacts are at the proposal-sent stage?
eval_questions.a: 215 (Stage S3 means proposal sent; counted after removing duplicates).

eval_questions.q: What is the total Amount of Closed Won deals with a Close Date in 2025?
What is the total Amount of open deals (not Closed Won or Closed Lost)?
Which rep owns the most customers, and how many?
eval_questions.a: KT (Kenji Tanaka) with 48 customers (Stage S5, after removing duplicates).

eval_questions.q: How many distinct contacts still belong to the rep who left the company?
eval_questions.a: 229 contacts are still owned by JM (Jordan Mercer, left in March 2026).

eval_questions.q: How many distinct contacts came in through the website?
eval_questions.a: 452, counting both "Web" (the old picklist value) and "Website".

eval_questions.q: Which lead source produced the most Closed Won Amount (join deals to contacts on trimmed, lowercased email, keep the oldest contact row, treat Web and Website as one)?
eval_questions.a: Website with $2,992,000.00. Unmatched deals are left out.
